content:
A professional headshot session with a photographer commonly costs $150 to $500, and more in large cities, before retouching, which is often charged per image on top. An AI headshot set generated from your own selfies costs $9 to $49 one time. The right choice depends on what you actually need the photo for, so here is what each option includes, what it leaves out, and what a single usable photo really costs.

Prices in this guide are typical ranges, not survey results. Photographer rates vary a lot by city, by experience and by what the session includes, so treat the figures as a sanity check and get a written quote before you book.

How much do professional headshots cost in 2026?

Typically $150 to $500 for a photographer session, with studios in large cities often charging more, plus retouching that is frequently billed per image. That fee usually buys 20 to 60 minutes of shooting, a proof gallery, and a small number of finished files. An AI headshot set from your own selfies costs $9 for 5 headshots, $29 for 25, or $49 for 60, paid once, with no session to attend and delivery by email in about an hour.

What does a photographer's session fee actually include?

You are paying for a person's time, skill and equipment, not for a file. A typical session fee covers a fixed shooting window, usually 20 to 60 minutes, the photographer's setup and lighting, a proof gallery to choose from, and a small number of finished images, often one to five. Anything beyond that is normally an add-on.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics puts median photographer pay at $44,660 a year, or $21.47 an hour, and reports that 67 percent of the roughly 145,000 photographers working in 2025 are self-employed. That is the key to understanding the price. A self-employed photographer has to cover studio rent, camera bodies, lenses, lighting, insurance, editing software and the unpaid hours between bookings out of each session fee.

So when a session feels expensive for half an hour of work, remember that the half hour is the visible part. The editing, the admin and the slow weeks are all folded into what you pay.

What costs extra with a photographer?

The session fee is the headline number, but the total is usually higher once you add the pieces most people need. Ask about each of these before you book, because the answers vary from studio to studio.

  • Retouching per image. Many photographers include one or two retouched files and charge for each additional one. This is where a $200 session becomes a $300 bill if you want five finished photos.
  • Extra looks. Changing outfits or backgrounds is often a separate tier, because it adds time and setup.
  • Usage licences. Some photographers price personal use and commercial use differently. If you want the photo on a company website, in a press kit or in print, check whether that is included.
  • Travel. An on-location shoot at your office usually carries a travel or setup fee on top of the session.
  • Rush delivery. Standard turnaround is often one to two weeks. Needing the files in 48 hours can cost more.

None of this is a criticism of photographers. Each item represents real time or real risk on their side. It just means the quote you compare against should be the full quote, not the starting price.

What are the hidden costs of a headshot session?

The biggest cost of a photographer is not on the invoice. It is your time. A studio session means finding a slot that works for both of you, travelling there, waiting, shooting, travelling back, and then waiting again for the edited files, which typically arrive a week or two later.

For most people that is a half day gone, and if you are self-employed or on a tight schedule, that half day has a price of its own. Reshoots are the other hidden cost. If you look tired, the lighting did not suit you, or your expression was stiff, you either pay again or live with it.

There is also a quieter cost: you get very few attempts. Research from the University of York published in PNAS found that first impressions vary substantially across different photos of the same person, with lighting, pose and expression all shifting how trustworthy or competent someone appears.

A session that hands you three finished images gives you three rolls of that dice. A set of 25 or 60 gives you far more to choose from.

How much does an AI headshot cost per usable photo?

This is the comparison that matters, because nobody uses every frame from any shoot. With a photographer, a $200 session that includes two retouched images and charges for extras might land you at $250 to $300 for four or five finished photos. That is roughly $50 to $75 per usable photo, and often more in a large city.

With an AI set the arithmetic runs the other way. The Pro plan gives you 25 headshots for $29, so even if you only love a third of them, you are paying around $3.50 per photo you would happily use. The Premium plan gives 60 for $49, which at the same hit rate is under $2.50 per keeper, and the Starter plan gives 5 for $9.

The honest caveat is that an AI set depends entirely on the selfies you upload. Picturesk asks for 5 to 15 recent photos of you, with 10 to 12 being the sweet spot, and screens every photo before payment so you are told which ones fail and can swap them. Good input is the whole game, and it is the one thing you control.

When is a photographer worth the money?

Quite often, and it is worth being clear about when. A photographer is the right call when the brief is creative rather than standard, when you need more than a head and shoulders frame, or when a group of people has to be shot together in one room.

  • A creative brief. If you need a specific location, props, a particular mood or art direction, a person behind the camera can respond to that in the moment.
  • Groups and team photos. Everyone in one frame, at one time, is a photographer's job.
  • Full body and environmental portraits. AI headshots are head and shoulders, square 1:1. If you need a full length shot on a factory floor, book the shoot.
  • Brand shoots. A campaign with lifestyle shots, product in hand and a consistent look across dozens of images is a production, not a headshot.

If, on the other hand, you need a clean, current, professional head and shoulders photo for LinkedIn, a CV or resume, a company page or a speaker bio, and you need it this week, an AI headshot generator does that job for a fraction of the price. We have a longer breakdown of process, timelines and quality in our AI headshots versus photographer comparison.

Is a professional headshot worth paying for at all?

Yes, at either price point, because the photo does work for you long after you have paid for it. LinkedIn's own sales team reports that members with a profile photo get up to 21 times more profile views and 9 times more connection requests than members without one. That is the difference between being considered and being skipped.

The quality of that photo matters too, and it matters fast. Princeton psychologists found that people form judgements about a face, including trustworthiness and competence, after about 100 milliseconds of exposure, and longer looks mostly make them more confident rather than changing their minds. A phone selfie taken in bad light is being judged in that same tenth of a second.

So the question is not whether to spend money on a headshot, but how much of the job you need done. A standard professional photo that looks like you, delivered fast, is a $9 to $49 problem now. A creative shoot, a group, or a full brand campaign is still a photographer's job and is worth their rate.

How do the Picturesk plans compare?

There are three plans and they differ by how many headshots you get and how much choice you have over the look. Every plan is a single payment, and every plan delivers full resolution images by email in about an hour.

  • Starter, $9: 5 headshots, 1 outfit, 2 backgrounds, standard queue. Enough for a single LinkedIn or CV photo if your selfies are good.
  • Pro, $29: 25 headshots, 3 outfits, 4 backgrounds, priority queue. The most popular plan, because 25 frames across a few looks almost always contains several keepers.
  • Premium, $49: 60 headshots, all 8 outfits, all 11 backgrounds, front of the queue. For anyone who wants a different photo for LinkedIn, the company site, a speaker bio and print.

Two guarantees sit behind all three. If a generation run fails, the refund is issued automatically. If the results do not look like you, reply to the delivery email within 3 days and you get a full refund, and you keep the images either way.
